sources.quote: Gives Lakkja initials, finals and 'Tones. Tone categories: 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8; Tone values: 51 231 24 11 55 214 24/55 11/24. Tones 7 and 8 have two values each [by vowel length]...'; 'Aspirated initials and voiceless nasals occur only with odd-numbered tones.' No statement about stress anywhere in the Lakkja section (only 'stress' hit in the volume is the gloss 'distress').

sources.quote: 'Proto-Lakkja has four tones, namely *A, *B, *C and *D like Proto-Tai... modern Lakkja dialects have six tones, namely A1, A2, B1, B2, C1 and C2 tones, and checked syllables that used to have proto-tone D have four tones, depending upon the initial and the vocalic length.' Comparative reconstruction; no mention of stress or accent in the pages read.

sources.note: The only other book-length grammar (Glottolog 'grammar', 271 pp) with a 语音 chapter; would show whether the Chinese descriptive tradition records any 轻重音 pattern in Lakkja disyllables/compounds that Fan's one-sentence stress remark leaves open. Fan (p. 30) calls its phonology brief, so low expected yield.
